terra.problem: The parking comparison blends a modern scene with the biblical setting by adding sandals.
The cookie comparison does not make sense: a remembered mountain name has no clear connection to a cookie needing time to settle.
The LORD says Esau's descendants will be afraid. Saying they are nervous here changes the future statement into a present feeling.
The blanket claim that nobody can claim a spot already taken goes beyond the LORD's stated reason for withholding Esau's land from Israel.
The cookie comparison is illogical: someone can ask for a cookie that belongs to someone else.
Saying Israel goes through Seir as customers presents payment as something that happened. The passage gives the instruction to pay but does not say they did.
The instruction to pay does not establish that nobody gives out free samples on the trip.
The passage does not identify the speaker of the parenthetical note, so attributing the comparison and its placement to Moses is a guess.
Israel's crossing does not establish that nobody hesitated or dragged their feet.
The LORD tells Israel not to harass or provoke the Ammonites when they get close. He does not tell them to keep their distance.
